count_foo1_foo2.title: Derive Exact Counts for Foo1 and Foo2
Derive Exact Counts for Foo1 and Foo2
count_foo1_foo2.prompt: Complete the four helpers in `analysis.c`. Count tuple-print calls separately from all `printf` calls. Use formulas rather than reproducing the printing loops.
count_foo1_foo2.hint: Foo1 adds one newline to each group of three tuple prints. Foo2 adds one newline to each row of n tuple prints.

help.concept: The exact tuple counts are `3n` and `n²`; total printf counts are `4n` and `n²+n`.
help.hint_1: Work from the traced values to an exact count before simplifying.
help.hint_2: Run the supplied test harness after each focused change.

checks.message: Foo1 has exactly three tuple prints per row.

foo1-reason.title: Why Foo1 is linear
foo1-reason.prompt: Why is Foo1 Θ(n) even though it contains two loops?
foo1-reason.hint: Ask whether the inner bound grows with n.

help.concept: A fixed inner bound contributes a constant factor, so 3n is Θ(n).
help.hint_1: Trace a small input or simplify the exact expression before choosing.
help.hint_2: Check whether the work adds, multiplies, or forms a changing sum.

help.concept: The n² tuple prints plus n newline prints give n²+n.

rectangle-animation.title: Fixed Strip versus Growing Rectangle
rectangle-animation.context: Watch the bound of the inner loop. A constant width contributes only a constant factor; a width of n creates a second growing dimension.

steps.title: Foo1: one row has fixed width
steps.body: For any i, j visits 0, 1, 2. The row width is always 3.

steps.title: Foo1: repeat the strip n times
steps.body: n identical rows, each with 3 tuple prints, gives 3n.

steps.title: Foo2: one row grows with n
steps.body: For every i, j visits 0 through n−1, so each row contains n tuple prints.

steps.title: Foo2: n rows by n columns
steps.body: Independent dimensions multiply: n rows times n tuple prints per row.
